title: Geometry — Common Core High School Math — Question Sets
id_format: S<set>-<section>-Q<number>. Section codes: M = MAIN (the course's own standard), B1, B2, ... = BACKWARD branches (a Grade K-8 standard, or a course standard that is the MAIN standard of an earlier set), F1 = FORWARD 1 and F2 = FORWARD 2 (standards of later courses; standard_course names the course). id is unique within this collection; uid = "GEO:" + id is unique across all collections. Forward branches name standards only, never question IDs of other collections. Set and branch numbers are fixed: they need not be consecutive, and an ID is never reused for a different skill (see revisions.json).

relations.main: the Geometry skill the set is built around (strand: core, or advanced extension (+))
relations.backward: a prerequisite obstacle to check when a student misses MAIN questions: a Grade K-8 or Algebra I standard, or the MAIN standard of an earlier Geometry set; branch.alignment is exact or supporting
relations.forward1: the next demand after MAIN; branch.progression is same-course deepening, cross-standard extension, or later-course extension, and branch.new_demand states what it adds
relations.forward2: a further demand; branch.builds_on says how it builds on FORWARD 1 (or why it is a separate extension of MAIN)
relations.nearest_related: true marks a forward branch that no standard directly continues; it uses the nearest related standard

grading_rules: Match each student response to its key record by the question ID printed on the question page (for example S40-F2-Q3). The page number is the same in the Question Collection and the Answer Key. IDs are unique within one grade's collection; across collections use uid (for example G5:S40-F2-Q3).
Multiple choice and true/false: the response is correct when the chosen letter equals correct_letter, or when the student wrote the text of the correct choice.

Short answer: accept any mathematically equivalent form unless the question asks for a specific form (equivalent fractions, decimals, and mixed numbers; a ratio written as a : b, a to b, or a/b; "x = 5" or "5"; terms of an expression in any order). Units are not required unless the question asks for them.
When an answer has several parts (separated by semicolons, or with labels such as "Rate of change:"), every part must be correct.
Drawing / plotting questions (type plot): correct_answer describes what a correct drawing shows. Judge the student's drawing against it.

Drawing + written questions (type plot_text): the student draws on the figure AND writes an answer. drawing_answer describes the correct drawing and correct_answer the written answer. Both must be correct: every requested point, segment or shape in the drawing, and the written conclusion.

Answer with required work (type work): required_method says what the shown work must use. A correct final answer without that work earns partial credit only; correct work with a slip in the final answer is also partial.
Explain / describe questions: grading_note says what a correct response must include; accept any reasonable wording.
grading_note also lists other accepted answers and the work behind an answer. It is guidance for the grader, not for students.

Geometry answer forms: the grading_note of every written answer begins with "Form required:" or with "Any" (for example "Any equivalent form" or "Any valid proof"), which says what else is accepted. "Exact" means an exact value (radicals, π, fractions); a decimal approximation alone is not full credit. When rounding is allowed the note names the precision; an answer within half a unit of the last required place is correct. Units are required only when the question asks for them or the note says so.

Proofs and explanations (type work, and written answers that ask why): grade the logic, not the wording or the format. A paragraph, two-column, flow, or diagram-based argument is accepted unless the question names a format. grading_note lists the ESSENTIAL steps (every one must appear, with a valid reason), accepted alternative approaches, and common INVALID arguments (each earns no credit for that step): reasoning from how the diagram looks, measuring a drawing as proof of a general theorem, assuming what is to be proved (circular reasoning), or citing a theorem that depends on the result being proved.

Constructions (type plot): the construction must show its evidence: compass arcs and straightedge lines (or the folds, string marks, or software steps the question allows). A figure that only looks right, with no construction marks, is not full credit. Drawing tolerance: points within about 2 mm and angles within about 2° of the exact construction.

Drawings and graphs: correct_answer (or drawing_answer) states the geometric relationships a correct drawing must show (image vertices, lines, marks). Accept any drawing with those relationships; exact pencil position is not graded.
Every question has an explanation in its grading_note after the form rule; for numeric questions it shows the verified exact value and the work.
markup: prompt is plain text. prompt_markup uses {a/b} for a stacked fraction and 2{1/2} for a mixed number.
